content.prompt:
The continuous random variable $X$ has cumulative distribution function
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0,\\\dfrac{x^2+2x}{24},&0\le x\le4,\\1,&x>4.\end{cases}$$
Find the PDF $f(x)$ of $X$, stating its values for all $x$.

answer.worked:
The PDF is the derivative of the CDF. For $0<x<4$,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=F'(x)\\f(x)&=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^2+2x}{24}\right)\\f(x)&=\frac{2x+2}{24}\\f(x)&=\frac{x+1}{12}.\end{align*}$$
For $x<0$ and $x>4$, $F(x)$ is constant, so $f(x)=0$.
Hence $f(x)=\frac{x+1}{12}$ for $0\le x\le4$, and $0$ otherwise.

content.prompt: Find the cumulative distribution function for each continuous probability distribution.

answer.worked:
For $0\le x\le3$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{t^2}{9}\,dt\\F(x)&=\frac19\left[\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^x\\F(x)&=\frac{x^3}{27}.\end{align*}$$
Outside this interval, $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>3$.

For $0\le x\le4$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{e^t}{e^4-1}\,dt\\F(x)&=\frac{1}{e^4-1}\left[e^t\right]_0^x\\F(x)&=\frac{e^x-1}{e^4-1}.\end{align*}$$
Outside this interval, $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>4$.

For $2\le x\le7$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_2^x\frac{4(t-2)^3}{625}\,dt\\F(x)&=\left[\frac{(t-2)^4}{625}\right]_2^x\\F(x)&=\frac{(x-2)^4}{625}.\end{align*}$$
Outside this interval, $F(x)=0$ for $x<2$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>7$.

For $2\le x\le5$:
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\int_2^x\frac{3t(8-t)}{135}\,dt\\F(x)&=\frac{3}{135}\left[4t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_2^x\\F(x)&=\frac{3}{135}\left(4x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}-16+\frac83\right)\\F(x)&=\frac{12x^2-x^3-40}{135}.\end{align*}$$
Outside this interval, $F(x)=0$ for $x<2$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x>5$.

content.prompt: Each graph shows a PDF. Use area formulae to find the CDF.

answer.worked:
The line has gradient $-\frac18$, so $f(x)=\dfrac{4-x}{8}$. The area from $0$ to $x$ is a trapezoid with parallel sides $\frac12$ and $\frac{4-x}{8}$ and width $x$.
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac12\left(\frac12+\frac{4-x}{8}\right)x\\&=\frac12\cdot\frac{8-x}{8}\cdot x\\&=\frac{x(8-x)}{16}\end{align*}$$
Check: $F(4)=1$.

For $0\le x\le2$, the line through the origin and $(2,\frac14)$ is $f(x)=\frac x8$. The area is a triangle with base $x$ and height $\frac x8$.
$$F(x)=\frac12\cdot x\cdot\frac x8=\frac{x^2}{16}.$$
So $F(2)=\frac14$. For $2\le x\le5$, add a rectangle of width $x-2$ and height $\frac14$.
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac14+\frac14(x-2)\\&=\frac{x-1}{4}\end{align*}$$
Check: $F(5)=1$.

A probability density function is defined piecewise by
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}k(4+x)&-4\le x\le0,\\k(4-x)&0\le x\le4.\end{cases}$$

answer.worked:
Split the integral at the change in the piecewise definition.
$$\begin{align*}\int_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,dx&=1\\\int_{-4}^{0}k(4+x)\,dx+\int_{0}^{4}k(4-x)\,dx&=1\\k\left[4x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{-4}^{0}+k\left[4x-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{4}&=1\\k\big((0+0)-(-16+8)\big)+k\big((16-8)-(0-0)\big)&=1\\8k+8k&=1\\16k&=1\\k&=\frac1{16}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac1{16}(4+x)&-4\le x\le0,\\\frac1{16}(4-x)&0\le x\le4.\end{cases}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the CDF, which is the probability of finding the chicken a distance of $x$ metres or less from the centre of the enclosure. $F(x)=P(X\le x)$.

answer.worked:
For $0\le x\le6$, uniform position within the enclosure gives
$$\begin{align*}F(x)&=\frac{\text{area of inner circle}}{\text{area of whole circle}}\\F(x)&=\frac{\pi x^2}{\pi\times6^2}\\F(x)&=\frac{x^2}{36}.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}P(X\le6)&=F(6)\\P(X\le6)&=\frac{1}{36}(6)^2\\P(X\le6)&=1.\end{align*}$$
This makes sense because the enclosure has radius $6$ m, so the chicken must be within $6$ m of its centre.

$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=F'(x)\\f(x)&=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x^2}{36}\right)\\f(x)&=\frac{x}{18}.\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $P(X\le1)=\dfrac5{32}$ and $P(X>1)=\dfrac{27}{32}$. These complementary events cover all possible values of $X$.

$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 1-e^{-0.01x}, & x \ge 0 \\ 0, & x < 0 \end{cases}$$

x &= \frac{\ln(0.01)}{-0.01} \\
x &= -100 \ln(0.01) \\
x &= 460.517...
\end{align*}$$
Rounded to two decimal places, the light bulb should work for $460.52$ hours.

$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{for } x < 0, \\ \frac{1}{3}x^2(4-x^2) & \text{for } 0 \le x \le 1, \\ 1 & \text{for } x > 1. \end{cases}$$

answer.worked:
The probability can be found using the complement and the cumulative distribution function:
$$\begin{align*}
P(X > 0.6) &= 1 - P(X \le 0.6) \\
&= 1 - F(0.6) \\
&= 1 - \frac{1}{3}(0.6)^2(4 - 0.6^2) \\
&= 1 - \frac{1}{3}(0.36)(4 - 0.36) \\
&= 1 - 0.12(3.64) \\
&= 1 - 0.4368 \\
&= 0.5632
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the probability density function $f(x)$ of $X$.

answer.worked:
The probability density function $f(x)$ is the derivative of the CDF $F(x)$. Expand the expression for easier differentiation:
$$\begin{align*}
F(x) &= \frac{4}{3}x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x^4
\end{align*}$$
Differentiate with respect to $x$ for the domain $0 \le x \le 1$:
$$\begin{align*}
f(x) &= \frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{4}{3}x^2 - \frac{1}{3}x^4 \right) \\
&= \frac{8}{3}x - \frac{4}{3}x^3
\end{align*}$$
For $x < 0$ and $x > 1$, $f(x) = 0$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Determine the mode of the distribution.
Give your answer correct to three decimal places.

answer.worked:
The mode is the value of $x$ that maximises the probability density function $f(x)$. Find the stationary points of $f(x)$ by setting its derivative to $0$:
$$\begin{align*}
f'(x) &= \frac{8}{3} - 4x^2 \\
0 &= \frac{8}{3} - 4x^2 \\
4x^2 &= \frac{8}{3} \\
x^2 &= \frac{2}{3} \\
x &= \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \quad \text{(since } 0 \le x \le 1\text{)} \\
x &\approx 0.81649\dots
\end{align*}$$
To the three decimal places, the mode is $0.816$.

content.prompt:
The time in minutes that a customer spends waiting in a queue has a probability density function:
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x(k-x)}{36} & \text{for } 0 \leq x \leq k \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the value of $k$ is $6$.

answer.worked:
For $f(x)$ to be a valid probability density function, the area under the curve must equal $1$:
$$\begin{align*}
\int_0^k \frac{kx - x^2}{36} \, dx &= 1 \\
\frac{1}{36} \left[ \frac{kx^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_0^k &= 1 \\
\frac{1}{36} \left( \frac{k^3}{2} - \frac{k^3}{3} \right) &= 1 \\
\frac{1}{36} \left( \frac{3k^3 - 2k^3}{6} \right) &= 1 \\
\frac{k^3}{216} &= 1 \\
k^3 &= 216 \\
k &= \sqrt[3]{216} \\
k &= 6
\end{align*}$$

The PDF $f(x) = \frac{x(6-x)}{36}$ is a parabola opening downwards with roots at $x = 0$ and $x = 6$.
Since the distribution is perfectly symmetrical about $x = 3$, the expected value is the axis of symmetry:
$E(X) = 3$

The variance is given by $Var(X) = E(X^2) - (E(X))^2$.
First, calculate $E(X^2)$:
$$\begin{align*}
E(X^2) &= \int_0^6 x^2 \left( \frac{6x - x^2}{36} \right) \, dx \\
&= \frac{1}{36} \int_0^6 (6x^3 - x^4) \, dx \\
&= \frac{1}{36} \left[ \frac{6x^4}{4} - \frac{x^5}{5} \right]_0^6 \\
&= \frac{1}{36} \left[ \frac{3(6^4)}{2} - \frac{6^5}{5} \right] \\
&= \frac{1}{36} \left( \frac{3(1296)}{2} - \frac{7776}{5} \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{36} \left( 1944 - 1555.2 \right) \\
&= \frac{1}{36} (388.8) \\
&= 10.8
\end{align*}$$
Now calculate $Var(X)$:
$$\begin{align*}
Var(X) &= E(X^2) - (E(X))^2 \\
&= 10.8 - 3^2 \\
&= 10.8 - 9 \\
&= 1.8
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
A function $f(x)$ is defined as
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}0, & \text{for } x<0 \\ 1-\frac{x}{h}, & \text{for } 0\le x\le h \\ 0, & \text{for } x>h\end{cases}$$
where $h$ is a constant.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the value of $h$ such that $f(x)$ is a probability density function.

answer.worked:
For $f(x)$ to be a probability density function, the total area under the curve must equal $1$.
The graph of $y = 1 - \frac{x}{h}$ for $0 \le x \le h$ forms a right-angled triangle with a height of $1$ (when $x=0$) and a base of $h$ (the $x$-intercept is at $h$).
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \\
1 &= \frac{1}{2} \times h \times 1 \\
1 &= \frac{h}{2} \\
h &= 2
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: By first finding a formula for the cumulative distribution function, sketch its graph.

answer.worked:
The probability density function is now $f(x) = 1 - \frac{x}{2}$ for $0 \le x \le 2$.
The cumulative distribution function, $F(x)$, is found by integrating $f(x)$ from $0$ to $x$ for the valid domain:
$$\begin{align*}
F(x) &= \int_0^x \left(1 - \frac{t}{2}\right) \, dt \\
&= \left[ t - \frac{t^2}{4} \right]_0^x \\
&= x - \frac{x^2}{4}
\end{align*}$$

The full formula for the cumulative distribution function is:
$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & \text{for } x < 0 \\ x - \frac{x^2}{4}, & \text{for } 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 1, & \text{for } x > 2 \end{cases}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Find the value of the median of the probability density function $f(x)$.
Give your answer correct to $3$ decimal places.

answer.worked:
The median is the value of $x$ (let's call it $m$) such that $F(m) = 0.5$.
$$\begin{align*}
m - \frac{m^2}{4} &= 0.5 \\
4m - m^2 &= 2 \\
m^2 - 4m + 2 &= 0
\end{align*}$$
Using the quadratic formula to solve for $m$:
$$\begin{align*}
m &= \frac{-(-4) \pm \sqrt{(-4)^2 - 4(1)(2)}}{2(1)} \\
&= \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{16 - 8}}{2} \\
&= \frac{4 \pm \sqrt{8}}{2} \\
&= \frac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{2}}{2} \\
&= 2 \pm \sqrt{2}
\end{align*}$$
Since the domain for the median is $0 \le x \le 2$, we must choose the subtraction ($2 + \sqrt{2}$ is approximately $3.414$ which is outside the domain):
$$\begin{align*}
m &= 2 - \sqrt{2} \\
&\approx 0.586 \text{ (3 decimal places)}
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
The duration of telemarketing calls to mobile phone users can be modelled as a continuous random variable $T$ minutes, with probability density function:
$$f(t)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{2}{5}e^{-\frac{2t}{5}}, & t\geq 0 \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere}\end{cases}$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine the cumulative distribution function for $T$.

answer.worked:
For $t<0$, $F(t)=0$. For $t\geq 0$:
$$\begin{align*}
F(t) &= \int_0^t \frac{2}{5}e^{-\frac{2x}{5}}\,dx \\
&= \left[-e^{-\frac{2x}{5}}\right]_0^t \\
&= 1-e^{-\frac{2t}{5}}
\end{align*}$$
Therefore:
$$F(t)=\begin{cases}0, & t<0 \\ 1-e^{-\frac{2t}{5}}, & t\geq 0\end{cases}$$

Let the median be $m$.
$$\begin{align*}
F(m) &= 0.5 \\
1-e^{-\frac{2m}{5}} &= 0.5 \\
e^{-\frac{2m}{5}} &= 0.5 \\
-\frac{2m}{5} &= \ln(0.5) \\
m &= \frac{5}{2}\ln 2 \\
m &\approx 1.73
\end{align*}$$
The median call duration is $\dfrac{5}{2}\ln 2$ minutes, or approximately $1.73$ minutes.

For a continuous random variable, the probability of any single exact value is 0, because infinitely many values are possible in any interval.
In other words, P(X = a) = 0 for all a.

Furthermore, because P(X = a) = 0 and P(X = b) = 0, including or excluding endpoints makes no difference when calculating the probability of a value lying within an interval.
P(a < X < b) = P(a ≤ X ≤ b)

The mode is the value of x at which the PDF reaches its maximum.
To find the mode, we find the PDF’s maximum turning point.

For a function that is always decreasing f′(x) < 0, the mode is the start of its domain.

A continuous random variable X has PDF defined on [0,4]: f(x) = 3x(4−x)/32
Find its mode.

entries.description:
1. Differentiate
f(x) = (3/32)(4x − x²)
f′(x) = (3/32)(4 − 2x)
f′(x) = (3/16)(2 − x)
2. Solve f′(x) = 0
0 = (3/16)(2 − x)
x = 2
3. Check domain
x = 2 is in [0,4] ✓
4. Check maximum
f″(x) = −3/16 < 0 ∴ max
f(0) = 0,   f(2) = 3/8,   f(4) = 0
∴ x = 2 is the mode.
